teaser: Marconi's deck on journalism as intelligence, built as a working vault: 78 event types, an ontology, 17 observations and a community tracker, all synthetic.
core_idea: Francesco Marconi argues that journalism's advantage moves to how it observes: delta science, an atlas of events with definitions and observable signals, a domain ontology and a persistent record of observations backed by evidence; built here as a vault app that follows his eleven slides on a synthetic data-center buildout, it shows that comparing each new record with the last is where the stories appear, that AI makes observing and comparing cheap while journalists keep the definitions, the checks and the judgement, and that a vault suits an observation desk because the history is versioned, the evidence travels with each claim and the read key opens it.

not a pile of articles, but a graph whose every edge has a date and a source

quotes.text: The shape is the deck's; the facts are fiction, and the vault says so first.

figures.caption: The observation desk's cover, in the deck's style: the headline, and a synthetic data-center campus drawn in pen and ink, with orange markers on the power station, the data halls, the water tower, the town and the reservoir. Every marker in the vault opens a record.

The ontology slide, working: six entities with their attributes and the six relationships between them, each entity drawn as a pen-and-ink vignette. Clicking an entity lists the observations that changed it.

Every observation adds to what the newsroom knows: four headline observations as folders, January to September 2026, and the full history below, each with time, subject, change, event type and the records it rests on.

The fractal semantic graph in the vault: the question opens into the actors and the campus, the campus into twelve event families, and here Power and utilities into its seven event types; the breadcrumb leads back up, and every node's details open on the right.

The knowledge graph, in time: the ontology instantiated with the campus, its buildings, the projects, the companies, the county, the water district and the residents, played one observation at a time; at the acquisition, the new relationship is orange.

What is this project changing for the community: the impact tracker by jobs, water, power, land and public commitments, each item a claim, a change or an open question with its record, and the article and alerts it produced.
